kitchen.introH2: The Kitchen Remodeler Down the Street
kitchen.answerFirst: B&B Associates has remodeled kitchens in Ambler since 2013 from an office and warehouse minutes away on East Welsh Road in Maple Glen. Most full kitchen remodels in Ambler land between $55,000 and $150,000+, and in a pre-1960 Borough home you should plan on $5,000–$20,000 of that going to wiring, plaster, and plumbing you will never see.

sections.h2: What an Ambler kitchen usually starts as
paragraphs: Ambler has three kinds of kitchens. In the Borough, the Victorian-era and 1920s–1950s homes have small, closed kitchens with plaster walls, a single window over the sink, and a back door that was never meant to be the main entrance. In the Upper Dublin neighborhoods around Fort Washington State Park, the mid-century colonials have a workable footprint but builder-grade cabinets and a soffit that makes the room feel a foot shorter than it is. Around Maple Glen and Spring House, the newer construction has the square footage and simply needs the finishes and lighting it was never given.

We have worked in all three for 13 years, which matters because the right kitchen for a Borough twin is not the right kitchen for a 1990s colonial. In the older homes we open the kitchen to the dining room where the framing allows it and run cabinetry to the ceiling to recover the height the plaster ceilings give you. In the newer homes the work is mostly layout: a real island with 42 inches of clearance, a proper lighting plan, and an appliance package the room can support.

sections.h2: What Ambler kitchen projects run into behind the walls
paragraphs: The number we tell every Borough homeowner first: in a home built before about 1960, plan on $5,000–$20,000 of the budget going to the house itself. The most common item is the electrical panel. Many Ambler Borough homes still run on 100-amp service, and an induction range or a 48-inch range needs dedicated circuits a full panel cannot provide. A 200-amp service upgrade in Ambler runs $3,000–$8,000 depending on the meter location and whether the utility drop has to change. Plaster comes next; it comes off in chunks and powder, and it has to be repaired by someone who knows plaster. Cast iron and galvanized supply lines in the older Upper Dublin colonials are the third item.

None of this is a reason not to remodel. It is a reason to hire a design-build firm that prices it explicitly. A good bid for a pre-1960 kitchen in Ambler has a line for electrical service, a plaster allowance with the square footage it assumes, and permit and inspection coordination with Ambler Borough or Upper Dublin Township included, because both will inspect the electrical and plumbing. We write our estimates that way so the number you sign is the number you pay.

sections.h2: Investment and timing for Ambler kitchens
paragraphs: A same-footprint refresh in a newer Maple Glen or Spring House home, with semi-custom cabinetry, quartz or quartzite counters, tile backsplash, and a designed lighting plan, generally lands between $55,000 and $75,000. Opening walls, moving plumbing, and building an island moves the project into the $75,000–$110,000 range. Full custom kitchens with inset cabinetry, natural stone, and professional appliances run $110,000–$150,000+. Older Borough homes add the behind-the-walls costs above on top of whichever tier fits the finishes.

Plan on roughly 12–20 weeks from the first consultation to the final walkthrough, including design, permitting, and 4–10 weeks of on-site construction. Because our office is minutes away, Ambler projects get faster response on site visits, material deliveries, and inspections than a crew driving in from across the county. The consultation is free, and you receive a fully itemized estimate before any contract is signed.

faqOverrides.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Ambler, PA?
faqOverrides.a: Most full kitchen remodels in Ambler and the surrounding Montgomery County area fall between $55,000 and $150,000+, depending on cabinetry, countertops, and whether the layout changes structurally. Pre-1960 Ambler Borough homes typically add $5,000–$20,000 for electrical service, plaster, and plumbing updates. We provide a detailed, line-item estimate before any contract is signed.

faqOverrides.q: Do I need a permit to remodel my kitchen in Ambler?
faqOverrides.a: Yes for electrical, plumbing, and structural work, which covers nearly every full kitchen remodel. Permits go through Ambler Borough or Upper Dublin Township depending on your address, and both inspect the electrical and plumbing. We file, meet the inspectors, and close out the permits as part of our standard scope.

bathroom.answerFirst: B&B Associates remodels bathrooms across Ambler Borough, Upper Dublin, Maple Glen, and Spring House from an office minutes away on East Welsh Road. Hall baths in Ambler generally run $38,000–$55,000, primary baths $55,000–$85,000, and spa-level suites $85,000–$100,000+, with older homes adding cost for venting, waterproofing, and cast-iron plumbing that a cosmetic update never fixes.

sections.h2: Why the 1950s and 60s bathrooms around Ambler keep failing
paragraphs: A large share of the housing stock in Ambler and Upper Dublin is 1920s–1960s construction, and the bathrooms in those homes share a set of problems. The exhaust fan, if there is one, often vents into the attic instead of outside. The shower wall was built on drywall or old mud-set tile with no waterproof membrane. There is frequently a window inside the shower that has not been sealed properly in decades. The result is a bathroom that grows mold no matter how often it is cleaned, and a homeowner who has replaced the fan twice without fixing anything.

Those are not cosmetic problems and they do not have cosmetic fixes. When we remodel a bathroom in one of these homes we vent the fan through the roof or the wall to the exterior, build the shower on a true waterproofing system, and rebuild the window opening so water has nowhere to go. That is the difference between a bathroom that looks new for two years and one that stays dry for thirty.

sections.h2: What we plan for in Ambler Borough and Upper Dublin homes
paragraphs: In the Borough's older twins and colonials, the bathroom is usually small, the drain stack is cast iron, and the floor has settled enough that a large-format tile will telegraph every dip unless the subfloor is rebuilt. We assess all of that during the free in-home consultation so the estimate accounts for it. Moving a toilet or expanding a shower into a closet is often the best money spent in these houses, because the original layout was drawn for a family that bathed once a week.

A bathroom remodel that involves plumbing, electrical, and often a window change is permitted through Ambler Borough or Upper Dublin Township, and both inspect the rough-in before the walls close. We handle the applications and the inspection scheduling inside our scope. Most Ambler bathrooms take about 5–7 weeks of construction once materials are on site; older homes can add a week if the stack or the framing needs more than expected.

sections.h2: Investment and where the money goes
paragraphs: A hall or guest bath done right in Ambler, with proper venting, a waterproofed tiled shower, a new vanity, and updated lighting, runs $38,000–$55,000. Primary baths with a custom vanity, expanded walk-in shower with frameless glass, and heated floors run $55,000–$85,000. Spa suites with steam, a freestanding tub, and large-format porcelain throughout run $85,000–$100,000+. Ranges reflect completed projects and depend on square footage, plumbing moves, and finish level.

Heated floors are the upgrade we would never leave out in a Pennsylvania winter, and in a small Ambler bathroom the electric radiant mat is a modest line item. Spend on the shower waterproofing and the vanity; those are the two things you cannot upgrade later without starting over. Every project includes a fully itemized estimate before any work begins, and the consultation is free.

faqOverrides.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Ambler, PA?
faqOverrides.a: Bathroom remodels in the Ambler area generally range from $38,000–$55,000 for a hall bath to $55,000–$85,000 for a primary bath and $85,000–$100,000+ for a spa-level suite. Older Ambler Borough and Upper Dublin homes may add cost for exterior venting, waterproofing, and cast-iron plumbing replacement. You receive a fully itemized estimate before any work begins.

faqOverrides.q: My Ambler bathroom keeps growing mold. Will a remodel fix it?
faqOverrides.a: Usually yes, if the remodel addresses the cause rather than the symptom. In 1920s–1960s Ambler and Upper Dublin homes the culprit is typically a fan venting into the attic, a shower built without a waterproof membrane, or an unsealed window in the shower. We vent to the exterior, rebuild the shower on a true waterproofing system, and rebuild the window opening as part of the project.

Kitchen remodels in Bryn Mawr typically run $55,000–$180,000+, with the stone and plaster construction of pre-1950 homes adding structural and electrical work that a newer colonial never sees.

sections.h2: What a Bryn Mawr kitchen has to live up to
paragraphs: Bryn Mawr is one of the most architecturally distinctive communities on the Main Line: Gilded Age estates, Collegiate Gothic stone houses, gracious Tudor and Colonial Revival homes, and a significant stock of arts-and-crafts bungalows that reward character-conscious renovation. The kitchens in these homes were built as service rooms. They sit at the back of the house, behind a swinging door, with a butler’s pantry between them and the dining room, and they were never intended to be the room where the family lives.

The remodel that works here respects the proportions of the house and then quietly rebuilds the room around modern life. True inset cabinetry, doors flush within the face frame, is the classic look of Main Line estate kitchens in Bryn Mawr and Villanova, and it is one of the reasons custom or top-tier semi-custom lines are the only routes that execute it well. Honed marble or quartzite, a range hood scaled to the ceiling height, and a lighting plan that finally gives the room daylight are the details that make the kitchen feel like it was always meant to be there.

sections.h2: What the stone hands us
paragraphs: Every pre-1950 Bryn Mawr house hands us at least one of these: a load-bearing wall exactly where the island wants to go, plaster and lath that has to be repaired by someone who knows plaster, an electrical panel that cannot support an induction range, or a cast-iron drain stack eighty years past its design life running through the wall you want to open. We assess all of it during the free in-home consultation, and an engineer sizes any beam before we price it. A wall between a Bryn Mawr kitchen and dining room is often carrying more than it should, and we would rather know that in the design phase than during demolition.

Lower Merion Township has detailed code requirements and a thorough inspection schedule for plumbing, electrical, and structural work, and it enforces them. Properties subject to historic overlay review add a submission we manage as well. All of that is part of our standard scope; you never deal with the Building & Code Enforcement Department yourself.

sections.h2: Investment and timing in Bryn Mawr
paragraphs: Refined renovations without major structural work in Bryn Mawr tend to begin around $55,000–$75,000. Full transformations with custom inset cabinetry, natural stone, premium appliances, and structural changes routinely run $100,000–$180,000+, and the larger estate kitchens go beyond that. What moves the number is rarely the finishes; it is the structure, the electrical service, and the plaster, which is why our estimates itemize each of them.

Design and selections take six to ten weeks because custom cabinetry and stone have lead times. Construction in a Bryn Mawr stone home runs 8–12 weeks on site, longer if a beam or a service upgrade is involved. We book six to ten weeks out, so a kitchen you want finished before the holidays needs a signed contract by early autumn. The consultation is free and the estimate is fully itemized before you sign anything.

faqOverrides.q: How much does a kitchen remodel cost in Bryn Mawr, PA?
faqOverrides.a: Kitchen renovations in Bryn Mawr and Lower Merion Township typically range from $55,000–$180,000+ depending on scope, structural changes, and material selections. Main Line homes often require additional structural coordination, electrical upgrades, and higher-end materials to match the quality of the home, which we account for in a detailed, line-item estimate.

faqOverrides.q: Can you remove the wall between my Bryn Mawr kitchen and dining room?
faqOverrides.a: Usually, yes. In pre-1950 Bryn Mawr stone homes that wall is often load-bearing, so we have an engineer size a beam during the design phase and price the structural work explicitly. Lower Merion Township inspects structural, plumbing, and electrical work, and we manage every permit and inspection inside the project.

A primary bathroom in a pre-1950 Bryn Mawr home runs $65,000–$100,000+ in 2026, and roughly $10,000–$20,000 of that is the house itself.

sections.h2: What a pre-1950 Bryn Mawr bathroom actually involves
paragraphs: Homes in Bryn Mawr, Gladwyne, Villanova, and Haverford built between 1900 and 1950 almost always hand us at least one of these: a cast-iron drain stack that is beautiful workmanship and eighty years past its design life, plaster walls that have to be repaired by someone who knows plaster, a wall that leaks because the original window was never flashed, and a primary bath that was last touched in the 1970s. A cast-iron tub under a window, a 32-inch shower stall, a single vanity, and tile that has outlived three owners is the room we walk into most often.

The right remodel here is not a refresh. It is replacing the stack while the walls are open, building the shower on a true waterproofing system, rebuilding the window surround in solid stone so water has nowhere to go, and running new supply lines so the water pressure the house has always struggled with is finally solved. In a 2005 colonial in Blue Bell those items would be close to zero. In a Bryn Mawr stone house they are the reason the job costs what it costs.

sections.h2: Design choices that suit Lower Merion homes
paragraphs: Spend on the vanity and the stone, because in a Bryn Mawr home the finishes have to carry the room’s proportions. A custom vanity in stained white oak with a honed quartzite top, a freestanding tub under the original window, a 60-inch-plus walk-in shower with a bench and a linear drain, and large-format porcelain floors over electric radiant heat is the primary bath we build most in Lower Merion. Curbless showers that do not look clinical are increasingly the request from homeowners planning to stay in these houses for decades.

Lower Merion Township inspects plumbing, electrical, and structural work on a thorough schedule and enforces it. Properties under historic review add a submission we prepare. We file, meet the inspectors, and close out inside our standard scope. Plan on 6–8 weeks of construction for a primary bath in a stone home, and six to ten weeks of design and selections before that because custom vanities, stone, and steam equipment have lead times.

sections.h2: Investment in Bryn Mawr bathrooms
paragraphs: Hall baths in Bryn Mawr generally run $38,000–$55,000 when done properly, primary baths $55,000–$85,000 in newer construction and $65,000–$100,000+ in the pre-1950 stone homes, and spa suites with steam, a freestanding tub, and heated stone floors $85,000–$100,000+. The difference between the ranges is almost entirely the house: the stack, the plaster, the structure, and the supply lines.

Every estimate is itemized so you can see those house costs as their own lines, not buried in an allowance. The in-home consultation is free and is the fastest way to get an accurate bathroom remodel cost for your specific room, because no two Bryn Mawr bathrooms hide the same things behind the tile.

faqOverrides.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Bryn Mawr, PA?
faqOverrides.a: A primary bathroom in a pre-1950 Bryn Mawr or Gladwyne home runs $65,000–$100,000+ in 2026, with roughly $10,000–$20,000 of that going to the cast-iron stack, plaster, and structural conditions the house hands us. Hall baths generally run $38,000–$55,000 and spa suites $85,000–$100,000+. You receive a fully itemized estimate before any work begins.

faqOverrides.q: Should I replace the cast-iron drain stack during my Bryn Mawr bathroom remodel?
faqOverrides.a: If the walls are open, almost always yes. Cast-iron stacks in 1900–1950 Lower Merion homes are typically well past their design life, and replacing the section you can reach while the bathroom is gutted is far cheaper than opening finished walls later. We inspect the stack during the consultation and price the replacement as its own line.

sections.h2: The two kitchens we see most in Lower Gwynedd
paragraphs: From the mid-century colonials near Spring House to the newer construction in Gwynedd Valley and Penllyn, we have worked in virtually every neighborhood in the township, and the kitchens fall into two groups. The 1960s–70s colonials have a closed kitchen with a peninsula acting as a fence between the cooking and the family room that was opened up years ago. The 1980s–2000s homes have the footprint and the windows; they were specified by a builder to a price, with raised-panel oak or maple, laminate or early granite, and a soffit above the wall cabinets hiding nothing but air.

The first group is usually a rebuild: take out the peninsula, remove the non-bearing wall to the breakfast room, and build one long island with seating on the far side so a crowd has somewhere to be. The second group is usually a refresh: remove the soffit, run new cabinetry to the ceiling with a proper crown, painted semi-custom doors, a quartzite counter, a backsplash to the underside of the wall cabinets, and a designed lighting plan with under-cabinet strips. The soffit removal is the single highest-return dollar in a Lower Gwynedd refresh.

sections.h2: How we decide refresh or rebuild, in order
paragraphs: Does the work triangle function, with clear paths between sink, range, and refrigerator and nobody crossing the dishwasher door to reach the trash? If yes, lean refresh. Has the house become open while the kitchen stayed closed? If the family room and kitchen are already one social space in practice but not in plan, lean rebuild. Are the cabinet boxes sound? Builder-grade boxes from the 90s are often particleboard, and if the sink base has water damage, replacing everything is cheaper than nursing it.

Is the electrical panel ready? Most Lower Gwynedd homes of this era have 200-amp service, which is good news, but induction and a 48-inch range still need dedicated circuits; budget $1,500–$4,000 for panel work if the panel is full. How long are you staying? Under five years, a disciplined refresh returns more of its cost. Over ten, build the kitchen you actually want. Permits go through the Lower Gwynedd Township Building Department, are included in our scope, and are not billed separately.

sections.h2: Investment and scheduling from next door
paragraphs: A same-footprint refresh in Lower Gwynedd lands between $55,000 and $75,000. A rebuild that removes a peninsula or a wall and adds an island runs $75,000–$110,000, and full custom kitchens with inset cabinetry and natural stone run $110,000–$150,000+. Our estimates are line-item, so the difference between the tiers is visible before you sign.

A refresh is about six weeks on site; a rebuild with a beam and relocated plumbing is closer to ten. Because we are minutes away, Lower Gwynedd homeowners can often get an earlier start date than a crew driving in from across the county, and same-day site visits when a decision comes up mid-project. The consultation is free, and the Ambler design showroom opens Winter 2026/2027 a few minutes from your door.

A same-footprint refresh of a 1980s–2000s kitchen runs about $55,000–$75,000; a rebuild that opens walls and adds an island runs $75,000–$110,000. sections.h2: The 1990s primary suite, and what it was missing
paragraphs: Most primary bathrooms in Lower Gwynedd’s 1980s–2000s colonials were drawn by a builder who gave the room a garden tub nobody uses, a 36-inch shower stall, a double vanity with a cultured-marble top, and a fan that may or may not vent outside. The square footage is usually there. The layout is not. The most common project we do in Gwynedd Valley and Spring House is removing the tub deck, building a 60- to 72-inch walk-in shower with a bench and frameless glass in its place, and putting a freestanding tub where it belongs, or leaving it out entirely.

These houses are far easier than the stone homes we work in on the Main Line, which is why a project this ambitious usually lands under $85,000. Drywall instead of plaster, PVC instead of cast iron, and 200-amp service mean the budget goes to the room instead of the house. That is the argument for doing the primary bath in a Lower Gwynedd colonial now rather than waiting.

sections.h2: What we plan for in Lower Gwynedd bathrooms
paragraphs: Moving plumbing is the decision that changes the estimate. Relocating a toilet or a shower drain in a colonial with a basement below is straightforward; over a finished first-floor ceiling it means opening the ceiling, which we price explicitly. Stealing space from an adjacent closet to get a real shower is frequently the best money spent in a 1990s suite, and we design the closet back into the plan so nothing is lost.

A remodel that involves plumbing, electrical, and lighting is permitted through the Lower Gwynedd Township Building Department, which inspects the rough-in before the walls close. We handle the permits inside our scope and coordinate the inspections. Plan on about 5–7 weeks of construction for a primary bath, with the vanity, stone, and glass ordered during a six-to-eight-week design phase so nothing waits on a lead time.

sections.h2: Investment and the upgrades worth making

Spa suites with steam, a freestanding soaking tub, and large-format porcelain throughout run $85,000–$100,000+.

Heated floors are worth it in a Pennsylvania winter and are a modest line in a bathroom this size. A curbless shower with a linear drain is the upgrade homeowners planning to stay long-term ask for most. kitchen.introH2: Your 1990s Kitchen Isn’t Broken. It’s Just 30 Years Old.
kitchen.answerFirst: B&B Associates remodels kitchens in Blue Bell, Whitpain Township, and North Wales from a few miles down Route 202 in Maple Glen. If your Blue Bell kitchen was built between 1985 and 2005 and the layout works, a same-footprint refresh at $55,000–$75,000 makes it look and function like new; if the walls need to move, you are in $75,000–$110,000 territory, and most Whitpain kitchens land between $65,000 and $100,000.

sections.h2: Why Blue Bell kitchens are a specific kind of dated
paragraphs: Blue Bell, North Wales, and the surrounding Whitpain and Montgomery Township neighborhoods were built out in a few big waves: colonials from the 1960s and 70s, then a large run of 1980s through early-2000s homes with generous footprints and builder-grade finishes. Those later houses are the interesting ones. They have good bones, real square footage, big windows, and kitchens specified by a builder to a price: raised-panel oak or maple, laminate or early granite, a soffit above the wall cabinets, and a peninsula that made sense when the family room was a separate room.

Twenty-five or thirty years later the cabinet boxes are usually still sound. The drawers might sag and the finish has yellowed, but nothing is broken, which is exactly why so many homeowners off Skippack Pike and Township Line Road live with it for another five years. The question that decides refresh versus rebuild is not how dated it looks. It is where people stand when you have eight of them over.

sections.h2: The refresh, the rebuild, and the mistakes we see in Whitpain
paragraphs: The refresh: we do not move a pipe. We remove the soffit, run new cabinetry to the ceiling with a proper crown, install painted semi-custom doors, a quartzite counter, a backsplash that runs to the underside of the wall cabinets, a lighting plan with recessed cans and under-cabinet strips, and a new appliance package in the same openings. Six weeks on site, and the room reads like a different house. The rebuild: take the peninsula out, remove the non-bearing wall to the breakfast room, build one long island with seating so the crowd has somewhere to be, run new electrical to the island, relocate plumbing for a prep sink, and have an engineer size a beam. Ten weeks.

The mistakes: keeping the soffit, which keeps the kitchen looking like 1994 no matter what you spend on counters. Refacing thirty-year-old builder boxes, a decision you make once and regret for a decade. And buying the island before the plan, because islands need 42 inches of clearance on every side and plenty of Blue Bell kitchens are eleven feet wide.

sections.h2: What it costs in Blue Bell, and when to book
paragraphs: Whitpain and Montgomery Township kitchens in 2026 mostly land between $65,000 and $100,000. Same-footprint refreshes run $55,000–$75,000, rebuilds with structural work $75,000–$110,000, and full custom kitchens with inset cabinetry and natural stone $110,000–$150,000+. kitchen.introH2: Kitchens for Berwyn and Devon’s Established Homes
kitchen.answerFirst: B&B Associates remodels kitchens across Berwyn, Devon, and all of Tredyffrin and Easttown Townships, about 30 minutes from our Maple Glen office, with township permits handled in scope. Kitchen renovations in Berwyn typically range from $55,000–$180,000+, and because the housing stock blends gracious older homes with newer construction, budgets here span a wider range than almost anywhere else on the Main Line.

sections.h2: Three kinds of Berwyn kitchens
paragraphs: Berwyn and the broader Tredyffrin Township community sit in the heart of the Main Line, where brick colonials, stone ranches, and Chester County farmhouses line the streets of well-established neighborhoods, and where newer construction has filled in alongside them. That mix is why Berwyn kitchen budgets span such a wide range. A brick colonial from the 1950s or 60s has a closed kitchen with a serviceable footprint and dated finishes. A stone ranch has a single-story plan where the kitchen can open to the living space with one beam. A farmhouse has character worth preserving and a kitchen that was added to it twice.

In the colonials and ranches the project is usually a rebuild that opens the kitchen to the family room, adds an island with real clearance, and runs cabinetry to the ceiling. In the farmhouses the work is custom millwork, honed stone, and a layout that respects the original rooms while giving the family one place to gather. In the newer homes it is finishes, lighting, and an island the builder undersized.

sections.h2: Remodeling a kitchen in a house you just bought
paragraphs: Berwyn and Devon see a steady turnover of buyers moving into established homes, and the most common question we get is whether to remodel the kitchen immediately. Our advice: live in the house through at least one season before committing to a new layout, because where the light falls, where the groceries come in, and where people gather at a party are things a floor plan cannot tell you. The exception is anything unsafe or failing, an undersized panel or a leaking supply line, which is worth fixing right away and folding into the eventual remodel.

When the time comes, what these houses hand us depends on their era: plaster and undersized electrical service in the older stone and brick homes, load-bearing walls in the ranches, and settled floors in the farmhouses. We assess it all during the free in-home consultation and itemize it. Permits go through Tredyffrin Township, or Easttown Township for Easttown addresses, and we manage every application and inspection inside our scope.

sections.h2: Investment and timing in Berwyn
paragraphs: Kitchen renovations in Berwyn and Tredyffrin Township typically range from $55,000–$180,000+ depending on scope and material selections. Refined renovations without structural work begin around $55,000–$75,000; rebuilds that open walls and add an island run $75,000–$110,000; full custom kitchens with inset cabinetry, natural stone, and professional appliances run $110,000–$180,000+ in the larger stone and farmhouse properties.

Plan for roughly 12–20 weeks start to finish, including design, Tredyffrin permitting, and 4–10 weeks of on-site construction; older homes can add time if wiring, plumbing, or structure surfaces during demolition, which is why we assess thoroughly before committing to a schedule. The consultation is free and the estimate is fully itemized before any contract is signed.

bathroom.introH2: Bathrooms for Tredyffrin’s Colonials, Ranches, and Farmhouses
bathroom.answerFirst: B&B Associates remodels primary baths, hall baths, and powder rooms across Berwyn, Devon, and Tredyffrin and Easttown Townships, about 30 minutes from our Maple Glen office, with township permits handled in scope. Bathroom renovations in Berwyn generally range from $38,000 to $85,000+, with spa-style primary suites at the higher end and hall or powder rooms lower.

sections.h2: What Berwyn bathrooms start as
paragraphs: The brick colonials and stone ranches that fill Berwyn’s established neighborhoods came with bathrooms sized for a different era: a hall bath with a tub-shower combination and a 30-inch vanity, and a primary bath that is often a converted closet with a stall shower. The farmhouses have bathrooms added long after the house was built, with a cast-iron stack and plaster walls. The newer construction has the square footage and a builder’s garden tub nobody uses.

The primary-suite project we do most in Tredyffrin is stealing space from an adjacent closet or hallway to build a 60- to 72-inch walk-in shower with a bench and frameless glass, replacing a single vanity with a custom double, and adding heated floors. In the newer homes the garden tub deck comes out and the shower expands into its footprint. In the farmhouses the reachable stack is replaced while the walls are open and the shower is built on a true waterproofing system.

sections.h2: What we plan for, and the permits
paragraphs: The items we check during the free consultation are the fan venting to the exterior rather than the attic, the shower backing (drywall and old mud-set tile need a waterproofing system, not new tile), the subfloor under any large-format tile, the supply lines in the older homes, and whether a plumbing move sits over a basement or a finished ceiling. Each one that applies becomes its own line in the estimate.

All permit applications and inspection coordination with Tredyffrin Township are handled by our team as part of our standard scope; for Easttown Township addresses we manage those permits as well. Plan on about 5–7 weeks of construction for most Berwyn bathrooms, with the vanity, stone, and glass ordered during a six-to-eight-week design phase so nothing waits on a lead time.

sections.h2: Investment in Berwyn bathrooms
paragraphs: Hall baths done right in Berwyn run $38,000–$55,000. Primary baths with a custom vanity, expanded walk-in shower, frameless glass, and heated floors run $55,000–$85,000. Spa suites with steam, a freestanding soaking tub, and large-format porcelain throughout run $85,000–$100,000+, and the older stone and farmhouse properties add the stack and plaster work above to whichever tier fits the finishes.

Heated floors are worth it in a Pennsylvania winter. Curbless showers that do not look clinical are the request from homeowners planning to stay in these houses for decades. Every project includes a fully itemized estimate before any work begins, and the in-home consultation is free.

faqOverrides.q: How much does a bathroom remodel cost in Berwyn, PA?
faqOverrides.a: Bathroom renovations in Berwyn and Tredyffrin Township generally range from $38,000 to $85,000+. Hall baths run $38,000–$55,000, primary baths $55,000–$85,000, and spa-level suites $85,000–$100,000+. Older stone and farmhouse properties may add cost for cast-iron plumbing and plaster. You receive a fully itemized estimate before any work begins.

faqOverrides.q: Do you handle bathroom permits through Tredyffrin Township?
faqOverrides.a: Yes. All permit applications and inspection coordination with Tredyffrin Township are handled by our team as part of our standard project scope. For Easttown Township projects, we manage those permits as well. You will not need to interact with the municipality directly.
